newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling unchanged against the dollar.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling unchanged against the dollar.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was unchanged against the dollar on Friday but was firmer against the pound in a fairly active market, dealers said.
The Central Bank of Kenya posted a shilling mean rate of 56.20 against the dollar unchanged from Thursday. On the pound, it was posted at an average of 87.24 from 87.76 on Thursday.

A commercial banker said there was improved demand from the corporates leading to stability in the rates: "The shilling closed a dull session marginally stronger at 56.05/25 level having opened at 56.10/30."

A dealer said: "Exporter inflows continue to flood the market with very little interest from the importers. The shilling is facing resistance at the current level with the central bank intervening every time the unit heads towards the 56.00 level."
"The day's range is 56.05/25 with large inflows OFof forex anticipated as position squaring ahead of the weekend takes centre stage," she added.
Dealers said overnight money market rates held the 15-18 percent levels. The market has begun to feel the effects of both corporate and excise tax remmissions, they added.
Central Bank of Kenya Governor Micah Cheserem, a leading economic reformer, said on Thursday he expected shilling relative stability to continue in the near-term.
Cheserem said he was pleased that commercial banks "were behaving commendably", referring to a lack of acute speculative tendencies on the foreign currency market at the moment.

"I think we have got a stable currency now. That stability should hold," Cheserem told a gathering of the American Business Association (in Kenya). "The large shilling exchange rate associated with the major economic reforms of 1992 and 1993 is unlikely to be repeated."
